findings.question: q-biology-meiosis-and-genetic-variation-0001
findings.quote: A pair of matching alleles, such as $AA$, is homozygous.
findings.problem: The explanation discusses $AA$, which is a wrong choice. The review requires explanations to explain only the correct answer.
findings.fix: Keep only the definition of heterozygous and why $Aa$ has two different alleles.

findings.question: q-biology-meiosis-and-genetic-variation-0006
findings.quote: In mitosis and metaphase II, the chromosomes line up in single file.
findings.problem: This sentence discusses the wrong choices Metaphase of mitosis and Metaphase II. Those comparisons belong in their wrong-choice notes.
findings.fix: Explain that homologous pairs line up at the middle during metaphase I, matching the two pairs described.

findings.question: q-biology-meiosis-and-genetic-variation-0007
findings.quote: Which gamete can form only if crossing over happens between the genes?
findings.problem: The word "only" excludes other real mechanisms without stating an assumption. For example, a mutation changing B to b on an AB chromosome can produce Ab without crossing over between the genes. Gene conversion can also change one allele without a crossover.
findings.fix: Ask which new allele combination crossing over between the genes can produce from the stated homologs.

findings.question: q-biology-meiosis-and-genetic-variation-0007
findings.quote: Without crossing over, the gametes are $AB$ and $ab$, because each chromosome goes in as it is.
findings.problem: This explains the two wrong choices $AB$ and $ab$, contrary to the requirement to discuss only why the correct answer is correct.
findings.fix: Explain that exchanging DNA between the genes can put A and b on the same chromatid, producing an Ab gamete.

findings.question: q-biology-meiosis-and-genetic-variation-0007
findings.quote: This is a diploid genotype. A gamete is haploid and carries one allele of each gene. Check that a gamete does not carry both alleles of a gene.
findings.problem: The $AaBb$ note identifies the ploidy mistake and gives a check, but never explains why this choice looks right. For example, a student may copy both homologs into the gamete to preserve all the parent's alleles.
findings.fix: Add that carrying all the parent's alleles can seem necessary to pass both genes to offspring.

findings.question: q-biology-meiosis-and-genetic-variation-0008
findings.quote: These show two alleles of the same gene together. A gamete is haploid, so it carries one allele of each gene. Check how many alleles of a gene a gamete carries.
findings.problem: The note for $Aa$ and $Bb$ names the mistake and supplies a check, but omits why the choice is tempting. A student may split AaBb into two letter groups and mistake those groups for the products of division.
findings.fix: Add that splitting the written genotype into Aa and Bb may look like dividing the genetic material into two gametes.
